problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={e}^{x+y+z}+x+y+z$, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(0,0,0).$
worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(0,0,0)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(0,0,0).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(0,0,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x+y+z}+x+y+z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x+y+z}+x+y+z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{x+y+z}+x+y+z)\,k \\  & =({e}^{x+y+z}+1)\text{ }i+({e}^{x+y+z}+1)\text{ }j+({e}^{x+y+z}+1)\text{ }k \\ ∇f(0,0,0) & =({e}^{0+0+0}+1)\,i+({e}^{0+0+0}+1)\,j+({e}^{0+0+0}+1)\,k \\  & =2\,i+2\,j+2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $2\,i+2\,j+2\,k$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(0,0,0).$
